name: sodium glycerophosphate
uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE Glycophos is indicated as a source of phosphorus in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older as part of parenteral nutrition (PN) when oral or enteral nutrition is not possible, insufficient, or contraindicated. Glycophos is a phosphorus replacement product indicated as a source of phosphorus in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older as part of parenteral nutrition (PN) when oral or enteral nutrition is not possible, insufficient, or contraindicated. ( 1 )
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of Glycophos have been established in pediatric patients 12 years and older as a source of phosphorus as part of parenteral nutrition (PN) when oral or enteral nutrition is not possible, insufficient, or contraindicated. Use of Glycophos for this indication is supported by established safety and effectiveness of an inorganic phosphate product in adults with supportive pharmacokinetic data of Glycophos in adults [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Glycerophosphate is hydrolyzed by serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to glycerol and phosphate, and the activity of ALP is expected to be similar in patients 12 years of age and older. Glycophos contains aluminum that may be associated with central nervous system and bone toxicity [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.5 )] . Glycophos contains glycerophosphate which is hydrolyzed by ALP in plasma to phosphate and glycerol. Glycerol may increase plasma osmolarity. When prescribing Glycophos, consider the combined daily amount of glycerol from all sources (e.g., intravenous lipid emulsions) including Glycophos, which may increase glycerol exposure and lead to an increased risk of systemic toxicity. The safety and effectiveness of Glycophos have not been established in pediatric patients younger than 12 years old. Use of Glycophos in this age group may result in increased plasma levels of glycerol.
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS Glycophos is contraindicated in patients with: Hyperphosphatemia [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )]. Hypernatremia [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )]. Hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 )]. eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 or patients receiving dialysis treatment [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.2 , 5.3 )]. History of a hypersensitivity reaction to sodium glycerophosphate or any of the inactive ingredients. Reactions have included anaphylaxis [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.4 )] . interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS 7.1 Drugs with Effects on Sodium Retention Concomitant use of Glycophos with sodium-retaining drugs (e.g., corticosteroids, corticotropin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agents) may lead to edema due to fluid retention. Monitor patients for swelling and weight gain. If edema occurs, consider modifying the Glycophos dosage or discontinue the concomitant sodium-retaining drug [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.3 )].
